title: Good: decrypt.rs CEK wrapped in Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> prevents key material in heap dumps
description: smime-tree/src/decrypt.rs: the content-encryption key (CEK) is held in a Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> throughout decrypt(). When the Zeroizing wrapper drops, it overwrites the heap allocation with zeros. This is the correct defense-in-depth measure: if the process crashes or a heap dump is captured after decryption, the CEK is not present in memory. The pattern is applied consistently — the CEK is never copied out of the Zeroizing wrapper into a plain Vec. Worth noting because it is easy to forget and the consequence (CEK in a coredump or heap profiler output) is a real vulnerability for keys used across multiple messages.
